lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Saturday, eight a.m., on a bumboat to Pulau Ubin.
**Mr Tan:** Welcome to the **Great Ubin Orienteering Race**! One map, one compass. First team to the treasure wins my homemade **waffles**!
**Dad:** Relax, Kavya. No map needed. I have an **excellent sense of direction**. Ubin is... **that way**.
**Kavya:** Dad, that's Changi Airport. We just came from there.
**Mum:** Sorry, darling. I'm on **Priya's** team this year. I want those waffles.
**Priya:** See you at the finish, Team Kavya. Bring tissues.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the little brass box in Mr Tan's hand.
**Captain Needle:** **Captain Needle.** Magnetic compass. Seventy years at sea, and I have only ever looked **one way**.
**Captain Needle:** **North.**
**Ah Boy:** I'll spin you round!
**Captain Needle:** Spin all you like, lad. Still **North**. And your father is pointing **south-west**.
**Narrator:** True North. Episode 14: The Great Ubin Race.
**Mr Tan:** Checkpoint one, the bicycle shop! Each bike lock's code is the **reflex angle** between the arms of this signpost.
**Priya:** Easy. The angle is **130°**.
**Kavya:** Same angle, same protractor. I got **50°**.
**Outer:** Hello. I'm **Outer**. I read a hundred and thirty.
**Inner:** And I'm **Inner**. I read fifty. Two scales, one protractor, thirty years married. We always **add up to 180°**.
**Kavya:** So **estimate first**. That angle is **acute**, smaller than a right angle. It's **50°**, not 130°.
**Inner:** **Centre cross** on the vertex. **Baseline** along one arm. Count up from the **0** on that arm.
**Dad:** Got it. The code is **050**. Trust me.
**Kavya:** **Reflex**, Dad: the angle round the **other side**. Take the angle away from **360°**.
**Inner:** And to **draw 295°**? Draw its partner, **360° − 295° = 65°**, then label the angle on the **outside**.
**Mr Tan:** Excellent. I won't **protract** this any longer.
**Mr Tan:** Checkpoint two, the quarry! Construct triangle ABC: **AB = 7 cm, AC = 5 cm, BC = 6 cm**. Pass the compass!
**Captain Needle:** Captain Needle, reporting for duty!
**Madame Compassa:** He means **me**, darling. Madame **Compassa**. A **pair of compasses**. You are a needle in a biscuit tin.
**Madame Compassa:** Three sides: **SSS**. Rule **AB = 7 cm**. Open me to **5 cm**, point on **A**, and... arc!
**Madame Compassa:** Now **6 cm**, point on **B**, and... arc!
**Kavya:** The arcs cross at **C**. Rule AC and BC. A triangle!
**Dad:** Lovely. Let me rub out those messy arcs.
**Madame Compassa:** **Never!** The arcs are your **working**. Rub them out, lose the marks.
**Ah Boy:** I made a triangle from sticks! **3**, **4** and **8**. It's broken.
**Kavya:** **3 + 4 = 7**. That's less than 8. The two short sides can't reach each other.
**Madame Compassa:** The two **shorter** sides must add to **more than** the longest. **3 + 6 = 9**. Bravo!
**Priya:** Our card: **XY = 8 cm**, angle **X = 50°**, angle **Y = 65°**. No compasses.
**Mum:** Two angles and the side **between**: **ASA**. Two sides and the angle **between**: **SAS**. Ruler and protractor.
**Mum:** Angle Z = 180° − 50° − 65° = **65°**. Two equal angles: **isosceles**. So XZ = **8 cm**.
**Narrator:** Twelve noon. The teams are on opposite sides of the island. Hungry.
**Mum:** Let's have lunch somewhere **exactly the same distance** from both teams. Fair is fair.
**Dad:** Easy. **Halfway**. Trust me.
**Kavya:** Dad, halfway is in the **mangrove swamp**.
**Madame Compassa:** Darling, I'll draw you **every** fair place. Open me to **more than half** of AB. From **A**: an arc above, an arc below.
**Madame Compassa:** Now from **B**. **Same width!** Never change my width mid-dance.
**Kavya:** Rule a line through the crossings, **P** and **Q**. It cuts AB **in half**, at **90°**: the **perpendicular bisector**.
**Madame Compassa:** And every point on it is **equidistant**: the same distance from A as from B.
**Kavya:** On the map, **AB = 9.6 cm**, so **AM = 9.6 ÷ 2 = 4.8 cm**.
**Dad:** There's a café on that line, **5.2 cm** from us. How far from Mum?
**Mum:** **5.2 cm**. No measuring needed. Café it is. Your father's paying.
**Ah Boy:** My arcs don't meet! The line is **7 cm**. My compasses are on **3 cm**.
**Madame Compassa:** Half of 7 is **3.5**. Three stops short, darling. Open me **wider than 3.5 cm**. Four will do.

chapters.title: The shortest way to the sea

lines.cap: **Mr Tan:** Checkpoint four: the line that cuts this **136°** fork exactly **in half**. Compasses only!
**Madame Compassa:** **Angle bisector.** Point on the vertex, O. One arc that cuts **both arms**, at D and E.
**Madame Compassa:** From D, an arc inside the angle. **Same width** from E. They cross at **F**. Rule **OF**.
**Priya:** Two angles of **136 ÷ 2 = 68°**. And every point on it is the **same distance** from both paths.
**Ah Boy:** And half of that: **34°**!
**Dad:** Bonus point for touching the **shoreline**? Diagonal! Shortcut! **Trust me!**
**Kavya:** The **shortest** way to a straight line meets it at **90°**: the **perpendicular**.
**Madame Compassa:** From your spot P, one arc cuts the shore **twice**: G and H. Equal arcs from G and H cross at **K**, on the **other side**.
**Kavya:** Rule **PK**. It meets the shore at **N**, at 90°. Dad's slanting route is longer: it's the **hypotenuse**.
**Dad:** I found a spot only **35 m** from the lookout tower!
**Mr Tan:** The tower is **40 m** from the shore, measured **perpendicular**.
**Kavya:** Then that's impossible, Dad. Nowhere on the shore is closer than **40 m**.
**Dad:** I may have been standing in the sea.
**Priya:** **060°** from the old well. Why the silly zero? It's just **60°**.
**Captain Needle:** A **bearing**, lass: from **North**, **clockwise**, **three figures**. Every ship in the Singapore Strait says **060°**.
**Ah Boy:** North, clockwise, three. **N-C-3**!
**Kavya:** And it's **from** the well. **FROM = FEET**: feet at the well, North line at the well.
**Dad:** Trust me, I measured it: **72°**, **this** way.
**Captain Needle:** Anticlockwise! **Off course!** Clockwise, that's **360° − 72° = 288°**.
**Captain Needle:** The four points, clockwise: **N**ever **E**at **S**oggy **W**affles.
**Ah Boy:** Why would anyone eat **soggy** waffles?
**Priya:** And halfway: north-east **045°**, south-east **135°**, south-west **225°**, north-west **315°**.
**Mr Tan:** Last one: draw a bearing of **230°**.
**Kavya:** More than 180°. Turn to **South**, then **50°** more. Or go **130°** anticlockwise from North.
**Mr Tan:** Bearings. I find them very **bearable**.
**Narrator:** Four p.m. Dad and Ah Boy walked from the well to the drinks stall on **065°**.
**Dad:** Now we walk straight back to the well. Which bearing?
**Captain Needle:** **Off course!** That **reflects** you in the North line. You'd end up in the mangroves.
**Captain Needle:** Going back is a **half turn**: **065° + 180° = 245°**.
**Kavya:** **Under 180, add it on. 180 or more, take it off.** That's the **back bearing**.
**Mum:** Our card: Q from P is **298°**. So P from Q is **298° − 180° = 118°**.
**Ah Boy:** But **why** a hundred and eighty?
**Captain Needle:** Because North is North everywhere, lad. All North lines are **parallel**.
**Captain Needle:** **65°** at the well, and **65°** from **South** at the stall: **alternate angles**. A Z.
**Kavya:** So from North at the stall: **180°** round to South, then **65°** more. **245°**.
**Mr Tan:** Look up! A Changi runway: one end is **02**, about **020°**. The other end is **20**, about **200°**: the **back bearing**.
**Dad:** Two four five. **Trust me**, I knew that.
**Narrator:** Five p.m. Race HQ. The final clue, and a very small scientist.
**Dr Shrink:** **Dr Shrink!** I shrink the real world onto paper! Every length divided by the **same number**!
**Dr Shrink:** Angles? I **never** touch angles. That's why you can measure a **bearing** straight off a map.
**Kavya:** Our map says **1 : 25 000**. One centimetre on the map is **25 000 cm** in real life.
**Dad:** HQ to the jetty: **9 cm**. Times 25 000: **225 000 km**!
**Dr Shrink:** That's past halfway to the **Moon**, sir! It's **225 000 cm**, so **2250 m**: **2.25 km**.
**Kavya:** Map to real: **multiply**. Real to map: **divide**. And **1 km = 100 000 cm**.
**Mum:** The road back to the jetty is **1.5 km**. How long on the map?
**Mr Tan:** Final clue! From the big tree: **12 m** on **040°**, then **9 m** on **130°**. Scale: **1 cm to 2 m**.
**Captain Needle:** North line at the tree: **040°**, rule 6 cm. At the turn, a **new North line**: **130°**, rule 4.5 cm.
**Kavya:** Priya's running both legs. We measure the **shortcut**: **7.5 cm × 2 = 15 m**, on a bearing of about **077°**.
**Narrator:** Five-thirty. The treasure box is in a kampong garden. Next to **Gertie**.
**Gertie:** Meh. I'm tied to that post with a **5 m** rope.
**Ah Boy:** Can she reach the waffles?
**Madame Compassa:** Every point **5 m** from the post makes a **circle**. All the points that obey a rule: a **locus**.
**Kavya:** The box is **6 m** from the post. Outside the circle. Safe!
**Gertie:** **Less than** five metres: inside, dashed line. **At least** five: solid line. I've had time to think.
**Gertie:** Did I mention my rope slides along a **10 m rail**?
**Madame Compassa:** Then it's every point within **5 m** of the rail: two straight sides and two **semicircles**. A running track.
**Gertie:** Meh. Waffles.
**Mr Tan:** Tie-breaker! Construct **60°** with compasses only.
**Madame Compassa:** Arc from A, cutting the line at B. **Same radius** from B. They cross at C. **Euclid's** very first construction!
**Kavya:** AB = AC = BC: **equilateral**, so **60°**. Bisect it: **30°**. A perpendicular: **90°**. Bisect: **45°**.
**Mr Tan:** It's a tie! Both teams share the waffles.
**Gertie:** What waffles? ...Bit soggy, anyway.
**Ah Boy:** **Never Eat Soggy Waffles!**

chapters.title: The island saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before we go, the island would like to save you some marks.
**Outer:** One. **Estimate first.** If the angle is acute, it isn't 130°. Ask my wife.
**Captain Needle:** Two. **Three figures.** Not 45°: **045°**.
**Kavya:** Three. **From = feet.** Stand at the point after **from**, and turn **clockwise**.
**Madame Compassa:** Four. **Same width** from both ends. And never, ever rub out your arcs.
**Dad:** Five. **Convert your units**: centimetres to kilometres. Not to the Moon. Ask me how I know.
**Priya:** Six. A **new North line** at every turn of a journey. Parallel to the first.
**Narrator:** True North will return.
**Ah Boy:** I bought a souvenir! A fridge **magnet**!
**Captain Needle:** Seventy years at sea... and I have never seen **South**.
**Captain Needle:** It's beautiful.
**Dad:** Finally. A compass that agrees with me.
